_doc: GRANDFATHERED ledger rows: the ones that break a convention this repo now enforces but that
predate it and cannot be fixed in place. Read by scripts/programme-rollup.mjs.
ONE RULE COVERS EVERY SECTION, and it is why this is a file of RECORDS rather than a count: a
violation not named here is an integrity failure, and a record here that no longer corresponds
to a real violation is ALSO an integrity failure. A stale acknowledgement is the same shape as
the thing it was meant to expose, and a bare ceiling of 'four' lets a fifth violation move in
the moment one of these is superseded. Each record is keyed on identity, so the ratchet can only
ever be satisfied by the specific rows it was declared for. This mirrors
infra/template-parity-exclusions.yaml, whose own header makes the same argument.
WHY ANYTHING IS GRANDFATHERED AT ALL. The ledger is append-only and is never corrected in place
(PROGRAMME.md §3). Every remedy therefore lands on the NEXT row for a cell, never on the row
that is wrong — so between a convention being adopted and that cell being re-run, the old row
stands. Recording it is what makes the next one arrive visibly instead of silently.
SURVIVING CLAIMS ONLY. Both checks walk the collapsed view, for the same reason the
BLOCKED-vs-spent rule does: firing on a row that has already been superseded punishes the
supersession convention this repo asks people to follow. So exactly one record per cell can
ever match, and a duplicate is refused rather than absorbed.
THIS FILE IS NOT THE FIX FOR A NEW VIOLATION. Each section says what the fix actually is.
Ledger rows whose `git sha` column does not match the `git_sha` recorded inside their own proof
bundle. #2718.
THE DRIFT RUNS BOTH WAYS, which is what rules out every benign explanation. hetzner/full and the
two gcp rows name a commit NEWER than the run; aws/full names one OLDER. 'The row is written
after the code moved' cannot cover both. The mechanism is structural: provisioning-e2e.sh takes
`git rev-parse --short HEAD` in the ROLLUP job while the bundle's git_sha is stamped in the LEG
job, so any merge landing between them separates the two.
TWO OF THESE BACK CELLS THE GRID RENDERS PROVEN — gcp/byo (gitops) and gcp/day2. That is why
this is a guard and not a note: a PASS naming a commit its run never executed is unverifiable in
precisely the way an expiring CI run tag was, and every 2026-07-22 row was retracted for that.
THE FIX IS NOT A RECORD HERE. Supersede the row with a RETRACTED naming it, then re-record with
the sha the bundle carries — a proof decision with its own evidence, not a lint.

_doc: Red cells whose surviving ledger row names no issue in its last column. #3157.
AN UNOWNED RED IS THE ONE STATE THE GRID CANNOT RANK. PROGRAMME.md's 'mechanical next' orders
failing cells above never-run ones BECAUSE a red already carries a diagnosed cause. A red with
no issue has no diagnosis to rank on: it reads as work while being nobody's — strictly worse
than a never-run cell, which at least advertises what it is.
THE ONE RECORD HERE IS NOT UNOWNED, IT IS UNCITABLE. #3098 (`e2e nightly: azure RED (addons)`)
is open and is exactly this red. The row carrying the verdict is the 2026-08-25 azure/full
composite, written before this was enforced, and the ledger is append-only. The citation lands
when azure/addons is next recorded, and deleting this record is that run's job.
THE FIX FOR A NEW ONE IS NEVER A RECORD HERE. If the row is the one you are writing, put the
issue number in its last column. If no issue exists, file one — the nightly convention is
`e2e nightly: <cloud> RED (<dimension>)`, which the rollup already parses.
